reviewer: independent second-pass visual reviewer (Claude subagent, not the builder)

deductions.reason: End-block window frames are dark bronze with plain panes; photos (purdue_2018_facade, bsa_exterior, gallery_southeast_dean_2021) show white/off-white frames with transoms and divided lights.
No cast-stone heads and sills on end-block windows; ground-floor windows lack the stone transom panel at about two-thirds height (purdue_2018_facade, north-block west face).

South face of the south block reuses the north-face schedule of tall two-storey units. gallery_southeast_dean_2021 shows punched single and paired windows per floor, with tall glazed strips only near the ends.
Tall vertical stair-tower window strips at the junctions of the glazed range and the end blocks are missing (purdue_2018_facade, bsa_exterior). The model shows blank white panels there.
Glazed-range bays lack the small-pane upper lights on floors 2 and 3 and the deep dark-bronze projecting frame (purdue_2022_student_life, bsa_exterior).

West ground floor is storefront flush with the piers. The photos show a recessed arcade: free-standing limestone piers, storefront set well back, brick piers between storefront bays, and visible double doors.
Diaper (diagonal) brick pattern on the end-block upper floors is absent; it dominates the end-block faces in every close photo.
No exposed rafter/bracket tails under the deep end-block eaves; the soffit is a flat dark slab.
Name lettering sits behind the piers and is cut off ('MAS S. AND HA... D. WILMETH A...'). In the photos it runs continuously across the frieze over about five bays.
'W' brackets are simplified into angled blocks; the photos show W-shaped paired steel struts on each pier.
No projecting brick corner and bay pilasters on the end blocks (purdue_2018_facade north face, gallery_southeast_dean_2021).
Ground storey of the north block juts out and steps along the north face (GROUND polygon wider than UPPER), and the belt course follows the jogs. The photo shows a flush north face.

Spurious stone band at z 10.2-10.45 between floors 2 and 3 on all end-block faces cuts the tall north-face windows. The photos have no band there; the real bands are a string course above the floor-3 heads plus a frieze.
Eave edge reads as a thick flat slab with no gutter/fascia profile.
Downpipes hang from the eave edge about 1.5 m off the wall down to grade. The photos show downpipes fixed to the wall at pilaster lines (about 5 on the north face) with goosenecks to the gutter.
West-range eave underside shows red roof-tile material instead of a soffit finish (rv_G_V04_west_entrance).

Untextured white surfaces exposed on the exterior at the NW and SW range/block junctions, at the south-block east junction, and as a white box at the south-face ground floor. They look like the interior stair-tower/partition material showing through gaps in the exterior skin.
Brick is uniform warm red/pink. The photos show darker red-brown brick with dark burnt headers forming the diaper.
End-block window frame colour is wrong: dark instead of white.
Roof tile is dull brown-red; the photos (purdue_2017_day, bsa_exterior) show brighter orange terracotta.
Fascia/gutter is neutral grey; the photos show dark bronze to copper-patina edges.
Holes in the exterior shell exposing interior white walls.

r1 review renders place the ground plane at the basement level (z = -5), so every photo-matched view shows a 5 m blank plinth, and the 'eye-height' cameras (z 1.7) are really 6.7 m above the render ground. Re-rendered here at grade (rv_G_*).
Small stray object floating at about floor-2 level on the south face near the SW corner (rv_G_V09_southeast).
Truncated name text.

findings.required_correction: White/off-white frames with transom and muntin grid matching the photos; keep glass dark.
Add the diagonal dark-header diaper pattern to the brick fields of floors 2-3 and the frieze strip, as a texture or material.
Free-standing piers with storefront set back about 2.5-3 m, brick piers between storefront bays, double doors in the central bays, dark arcade ceiling.

findings.facade: Glazed-range/end-block junctions (NW, SW), south-face ground floor, south-block east junction
findings.required_correction: Close the exterior skin where segments are skipped. At the west junctions model the stair-tower bays as brick with tall continuous vertical window strips.

findings.feature: Eave brackets / rafter tails and gutter
findings.required_correction: Add regularly spaced exposed brackets under the deep eaves and a thin bronze/copper fascia-gutter in place of the thick slab edge.
Remove the z 10.2 band between floors 2 and 3. Add the string course above the floor-3 window heads plus the brick frieze and stone architrave under the eave.

findings.feature: Window stone heads/sills and ground-floor transom panels
findings.required_correction: Add cast-stone lintels and sills to every upper window and the stone transom panel on the tall ground-floor windows.
Use punched single/paired windows on floors 2 and 3 with stone heads/sills per gallery_southeast_dean_2021, with tall glazed strips only near the corners, plus the projecting end pavilions.
Bring the lettering forward of the piers onto one continuous frieze plane so the full name 'THOMAS S. AND HARVEY D. WILMETH ACTIVE LEARNING CENTER' reads; use dark bronze letters.
Attach downpipes to the wall at the pilaster lines (about 5 on the north face, plus corners) with goosenecks from the gutter; remove the free-hanging poles at the eave corners.
Add shallow projecting brick piers at the corners and between the window groups (north face, south-face pavilions).
Check the GROUND vs UPPER footprint. The photo shows a flush north face; remove the projections or limit them to the stone plinth.
Deepen the projecting dark-bronze bay frames, add the small-pane upper lights, model W-shaped strut brackets, and give the eave soffit a non-tile finish.
Brighten the terracotta toward orange-red (purdue_2017_day); the aerial is more muted, so aim between the two.
Optional: stone plinth blocks at pier bases and low stone planters/benches along the west plaza (all west photos).

uncertainties: Quick review (about 20 minutes), exterior only; interior ignored.
East faces have no photo coverage and were not scored in detail.
Colour comparisons are qualitative; lighting differs strongly between sources (sunlit summer vs overcast winter).
The identity of the white surfaces was inferred from the builder (exterior_walls skips west-facing segments at WEST_X; stair towers use the white material) and was not confirmed by raycast.
Whether the north-face ground-storey projection is real (for example a shallow plinth) could not be settled from the photos at hand.
